Bernoulli: A single yes/no outcome with a given probability, such as accept or reject, pass or fail, or rework or not.
Beta: A value between a minimum and a maximum with a flexible shape, such as a fraction, a proportion or a bounded time.
Binomial: Count of successes (for example defective parts) in a fixed number of independent trials.
BoundedNormal: Bell-shaped variation around an average, cut off at a minimum and a maximum so a time cannot go negative or beyond a physical limit.
Cauchy: Very heavy-tailed values with frequent extreme outliers in both directions; rarely right for times, and it often returns negative values.
ChiSquare: Statistical diagnostics and sums of squared normal variations; rarely used for simulation times.
Constant: A fixed duration that never varies, for a deterministic service time, transit time or interval.
CustomExpression: Any model expression, for example '2 + EXPO(3)', when no single distribution fits.
DiscreteUniform: A whole number between a minimum and a maximum, each equally likely, such as a random lot size from 1 to 6.
EmpiricalContinuous: Measured data as a histogram: a bin is picked by its weight, then a value is drawn evenly within it (a continuous draw, not a resample of points).
EmpiricalDiscrete: Whole-number values with their own measured probabilities, such as order sizes or the number of items per job.
Erlang: Time to finish k exponential steps in a row, giving a service time less variable than exponential but still random.
Exponential: Time between random independent arrivals, or time to a random breakdown, when past events do not change the next one.
FixedSchedule: Exact listed times, for arrivals or events that follow a fixed timetable such as a roster or a delivery plan.
Gamma: Right-skewed service or processing times that cannot go below zero, from very regular to very variable.
Geometric: Number of attempts until the first success, such as tries before a part passes inspection.
Hypergeometric: Successes in a sample drawn without replacement from a finite lot, such as defectives found when inspecting a sample.
InverseGaussian: Right-skewed positive times such as a reaction or decision delay, or the time for a drifting quantity to reach a level.
JohnsonSB: A skewed value that stays between a minimum and a maximum, such as a yield or fill percentage.
JohnsonSU: A flexible fit for skewed, heavy-tailed data when no simple distribution matches; it can return negative values.
LogLogistic: Right-skewed durations with a heavier tail than lognormal, such as repair or lifetime data that cannot go below zero.
Lognormal: Right-skewed times that cannot go below zero, such as manual handling, picking or repair durations with an occasional long one.
NegativeBinomial: Number of trials needed to get a set number of successes, each with the same chance of success.
Normal: Symmetric variation around an average, such as a cycle time that is rarely far from the mean; it can go negative unless the mean is much larger than the spread.
PearsonTypeV: Right-skewed positive delays or times to failure with a long tail, an alternative to lognormal.
PearsonTypeVI: A ratio of two gamma variables, such as cost per service, that is always positive; it can model times when the parameters suit.
Poisson: Counts per period, such as the number of arrivals or events in a fixed time window.
Rayleigh: A positive magnitude such as movement noise or a positioning error, with a single scale parameter.
Triangular: Min, most likely and max are known, usually from expert estimates when there is no data.
Uniform: Any value between a minimum and a maximum is equally likely; use it when only the min and max are known.
Weibull: Equipment lifetimes and time to failure, where the breakdown rate can rise with age (wear-out) or fall (early failures).
